findings.description: The nudge pays out the FULL nudgePaymentToken balance to a caller-chosen `recipient` on a purely count-based gate (`count >= nudgeSize`), with the payout decoupled from the value the caller contributed. This is a permissionless winner-take-all pot: a searcher who sees an honest qualifying batchMint in the mempool can copy it with `recipient = self` and a higher gas bid, pay for the same `nudgeSize` real mints, and scoop the entire externally-funded pot. The story-015 `minReward` floor does NOT prevent the front-run — it only lets the LOSER avoid minting for a sniped (now-zero) reward; whoever lands first still takes the whole balance-based payout. This is the historically-acknowledged M-01 and is a valid permissionless MEV finding under Law 1 (no principal loss; honest user still receives their NFTs).
presentMitigations: Pot snapshotted BEFORE the mint loop (story-016) — closes the donation-self-refund sub-vector; per-mint donations seed the NEXT claimant
Minter + dispatcherIndex pinned to owner state (story-013/014) — closes the original caller-supplied no-op-minter drain (run-12 H-01)
minReward slippage floor (story-015) — protects the loser from minting for a sniped reward
missingMitigations: Payout is NOT bounded by the contributor's own paid value
Recipient is NOT pinned to a non-caller address
findings.lawBasis: Law 1 (permissionless MEV on a legitimately-funded pot)

findings.description: Operational-hazard facet of the same winner-take-all design (Law 3 footgun, NOT auto-invalid). Funding a bonus pot is a normal operator action, but because the entire balance is released on a count-only gate, funding the pot with more value than the cost of `nudgeSize` real mints at the dispatcher's ramping price silently converts the 'bonus' into a net-positive drain: a claimant pays ~nudgeSize*price in mints (receiving NFTs of roughly equal value) and walks away with the full over-funded pot as pure profit, so the pot is raced to zero on every refill. A competent, non-malicious owner topping up the pot would plausibly be SURPRISED that 'fund the incentive' equals 'set a bounty anyone can sweep'. Surface as safe-funding guidance (keep pot value <= cost of nudgeSize mints, or treat each refill as immediately claimable), at honest severity — do not dismiss as 'owner-driven'.
matchedSignatures: nudgeAmount = balanceOf(address(this))  (full-pot, value-blind to caller contribution)
missingMitigations: No on-chain cap relating pot size to nudgeSize * mint price
No per-refill / time-boxed release that would bound the giveaway
findings.lawBasis: Law 3 (non-obvious owner footgun — in scope as operational hazard)

findings.description: `for (uint256 i; i < count; ++i) nftMinter.mint(...)` iterates a caller-supplied `count` with no upper bound and an external mint call per iteration. Pattern signature matches the DB MEDIUM template, but the realistic impact here is LOW: the loop touches no shared/growing array, the caller bears their own gas, and the dispatcher's geometrically ramping per-mint price makes a huge `count` economically self-limiting. No third party is griefable. This is the historically-tracked L-02 carryover; recorded so it is not silently dropped (Law 1 recall), at honest low severity.
matchedSignatures: for (uint256 i; i < count; ++i)  (caller-supplied unbounded count)
findings.note: Impact is caller self-DoS only, not cross-user griefing. Severity intentionally set below the DB template's MEDIUM. Confidence reflects that the PATTERN applies; severity reflects low real impact.

manualReview.description: batchMint has NO ReentrancyGuard (confirmed: ReentrancyGuard is imported only by NFTStaker). It makes multiple external calls — payment pull, forceApprove, a `count`-length loop of nftMinter.mint() each of which dispatches an ERC1155 mint to the caller-chosen `recipient` (whose onERC1155Received runs attacker code), the nudge safeTransfer, and the dust-refund safeTransfer. Payment-token accounting is contract-balance-based (snapshot/refund of the whole balance), not per-call escrow, so a re-entrant inner call could in principle sweep an outer call's funds. Analysis suggests this is LIKELY NOT EXPLOITABLE for theft: (a) the re-entry hook only fires into the victim's own chosen `recipient`, so an attacker cannot inject themselves into a victim's batch; (b) an attacker re-entering their OWN batch only moves their own funds; (c) the nudge double-pay self-reverts because the full-balance snapshot transfer in the outer frame underflows the drained balance, and the forceApprove(minter,0) set by the inner frame makes the outer loop's remaining mints revert. Routed to manual review per Law 1 (recall over tidiness) — uncertainty is about whether the vector APPLIES, and a fund-holding contract making external calls without a guard is a defense-in-depth gap worth a human/Tier-2 confirmation. Recommendation: add nonReentrant to batchMint regardless.
matchedSignatures: safeTransferFrom / safeTransfer / forceApprove + external mint loop with no nonReentrant
presentMitigations: Reward/payment tokens are owner-configured standard ERC20 (not ERC777); prime token is derived, not caller-supplied
Re-entry surface gated by caller-chosen `recipient` (attacker cannot enter a victim's batch)
Nudge pot snapshotted before loop; double-pay path self-reverts
manualReview.lawBasis: Law 1 (do not drop a plausibly-security-relevant gap; route to visible channel)

manualReview.description: `latestPrice = price.mulDiv(APY_PRECISION, r)` floors the per-mint price, and the floored value is then multiplied: `S = totalStaked * latestPrice`. This is a division-before-multiplication shape (floor on latestPrice propagates into S, then F, newRate, runway). The contract documents it as deliberate: every site floors in the protocol's favour (conservative for a reward contract), the absolute error on S is bounded by ~totalStaked wei against S ~1e27, and the project knownIssues explicitly accept 'Floor rounding via OZ Math.mulDiv ... conservative-for-protocol is intentional' and warn AGAINST flipping any site to ceiling. Recorded for visibility (Law 1) but assessed as an ACCEPTED known design decision, not a live defect.
matchedSignatures: latestPrice = price.mulDiv(...) then S = totalStaked * latestPrice
presentMitigations: All rounding is floor / conservative-for-protocol (documented invariant)
Error bound (~totalStaked wei vs S~1e27) is negligible
Explicit project known-issue accepting this rounding

ruledOut.reason: _syncBudget()->_updatePool() runs at the HEAD of stake/unstake/claim and settles pending at the OLD rate/OLD totalStaked before any share mutation; setTargetAPY calls _updatePool() before mutating targetAPY; rewardDebt reset after amount change so no retroactive accrual. All notVulnerableWhen conditions satisfied. Prior M-01/M-03 fixes hold.

_updatePool caps elapsed at min(now,windowEnd)-lastRewardTime; _safePay reverts on shortfall (no silent cap); solvency invariant balance == rewardBudget + committedDebt maintained across pull/topUp/safePay/emergencyWithdraw; MAX_TARGET_APY=0.5e18 bounds the rate. Fix holds.

Accrual strictly bounded to [lastRewardTime, min(now,windowEnd)]; totalStaked==0 returns early (no div-by-zero); _recomputeSchedule guards S=0 and runway=0; currentRewardRate returns 0 at/after windowEnd. Boundary operators consistent.

NFTStaker does not mint phUSD; it pulls via dispatcherHook.pull(). _updatePool is the single writer folding exactly elapsed*rate; payouts == settled pending. BatchNFTMinter's mint loop mints NFTs at the dispatcher's paid price, not free reward tokens.

Shares are NFT units 1:1 (not priced off totalAssets); no exchange-rate-from-supply. Donating reward tokens raises budget for all stakers (accounted via committedDebt invariant), it does not mint shares. No first-depositor inflation.
Neither contract is an ERC4626 vault; no asset/share exchange rate.

No yield-strategy routing in NFTStaker (that lives in stable-staker); principal is NFT units tracked separately from reward. BatchNFTMinter's balance-based refund 'donates forward' by design, no principal skew.
NFTStaker setTargetAPY is single-step and settles at the OLD rate before mutating; the two-step/100-block APY commit is phlimbo-ea, not this project.
balanceOf(address(this)) is used for the reward budget V and the nudge pot, not as a manipulable price oracle for a swap/borrow decision; no AMM reserves/slot0/TWAP usage.
No swaps. The nudge already has a minReward slippage floor (story-015).
All ERC20 moves use SafeERC20 (safeTransfer/safeTransferFrom/forceApprove); ERC1155 safeTransferFrom reverts on failure. No raw .transfer/.send/.call.
No narrowing casts; all arithmetic is uint256 (grep-confirmed).
No proxy/initializer; both contracts use constructors.
No delegatecall/ERC1967/proxy.
No ecrecover/ECDSA/permit anywhere (grep-confirmed).
No permit().
Only internal forceApprove(minter, max/0); no user-facing approve race. C4 QA/known regardless.
No Chainlink/oracle.
No Chainlink/oracle.
No ETH handling, no payable, no address(this).balance, no selfdestruct dependency.
No governance/voting.
No bridge/chainid/lzReceive/ccipReceive.
No timelock.
Reviewed boundary checks (windowEnd min/cap, count>=nudgeSize, remaining/DUST_THRESHOLD, nudgeAmount<minReward, block.timestamp<=lastRewardTime) — all consistent; no off-by-one found.
onlyOwner setters are trusted-by-design (owner is non-malicious). Generic centralization not reported; the only owner-action surfaced is the NON-OBVIOUS over-funding footgun (PATTERN-002).
